== Aristolochia gigantea ==
'''''Aristolochia gigantea''''', the '''Brazilian Dutchman's pipe''' or '''giant pelican flower''' ([[syn.]] ''Aristolochia sylvicola'' <small>[[Paul Carpenter Standley|Standl.]]</small>), is an [[ornamental plant]] native to [[Brazil]], Costa Rica and Panama.<ref name=":02">{{Cite web |title=Aristolochia gigantea - Plant Finder |url=https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=276777&isprofile=0& |access-date=2024-06-03 |website=www.missouribotanicalgarden.org}}</ref> Typical of subtropical [[Bahia]] and [[Minas Gerais]] [[vegetation]]. This plant is cited in ''[[Flora Brasiliensis]]'' by [[Carl Friedrich Philipp von Martius]]. ''A. gigantea'' and other tropical Dutchman's pipe varieties pose a threat to the [[pipevine swallowtail]]  butterfly. The butterfly confuses ''A. gigantea'' with its native host plant and will lay eggs on it although pipevine swallowtail caterpillars cannot survive on the foliage<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 17, 2021 |title=Aristolochia Gigantea: A Death Sentence For Baby Pipevine Swallowtails |url=https://monarchbutterflygarden.net/aristolochia-gigantea-kills-pipevine-swallowtails/ |website=monarchbutterflygarden.net |language=en-US}}</ref> because the leaves are toxic to the larvae.<ref name=":02" />

=== Cultivation ===
In cultivation in the UK - where it must be grown under glass - this plant has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref name="RHSPF2">{{cite web |title=RHS Plantfinder - ''Aristolochia gigantea'' |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/1577/i-Aristolochia-gigantea-i/Details |accessdate=12 January 2018 |publisher=Royal Horticultural Society}}</ref> It does not tolerate temperatures below {{convert|10|C|F}}. It can be grown from seeds or cuttings.

=== Morphology ===
It is a vigorous woody [[evergreen]] climber (vine). Leaves are simple with a cordate heart shape and a petiole. Inflorescence has a single zygomorphic (bilateral) flower that is bisexual. Contains 6 stamens that are fused to form a [[gynostemium]]. There is a syncarpous gynoecium present.<ref>{{cite book |last=Simpson |first=Michael G. |title=Plant Systematics |chapter=Plant Systematics: An Overview|date=2010 |publisher=Elsevier |isbn=978-0-12-374380-0 |edition=2nd |pages=3–16 |doi=10.1016/b978-0-12-374380-0.50001-4}}</ref> The face of the flower is oval with a fine network of pale pink or whitish veins on a maroon background.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Ziegler  |first1=Christian  |title=A Magic Web  |last2=Leigh Jr.  |first2=Egbert Giles  |date=2002  |publisher=Oxford Univ. Press  |isbn=0-19-514328-0  |location=New York  |pages=70–71}}</ref> The rear of the flower is globular. The throat is yellow.
